correctness.rationale: Crofton gives the exact finite-n deficit integral. The orthant identity is derived from Gaussian signs; fixed-z arcsin maximization gives p(z,theta)^n<=exp(-n z^2/pi). After z=t/sqrt(n), dominated convergence computes the beta-function constant for n->infinity. All quantifiers, sampling normalization, geodesic perimeter and exception sets are specified. Independent numeric hull reconstructions match the analytic integral; the proof does not rely on them.

originality.rationale: The 2022 primary study uses precisely the orthogonal spherical wedge but evaluates expected edge-count growth (4/3)log n rather than intrinsic perimeter deficit. The 2015 halfsphere work proves Crofton and mean-width formulas on a different domain; it does not provide the sharp wedge beta constant. The claimed contribution is the evaluated n^{-1/2} perimeter law and its exact finite-n integral; priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: A natural intrinsic metric of the same orthogonal-lune random hull studied for logarithmic facet growth has a different sharp n^-1/2 convergence scale and a completely evaluated nontrivial beta-function constant. The exact finite-n integral and the geometric identification of a one-dimensional family of nearly containing hemispheres give structural utility beyond a routine restatement of Crofton.
